_about: The ONE case table for the trip site's adopt/release rules (server/control-plane-auth.js; adopt, release and, since S2, provision). It is run against the REAL site by tests/control-plane-binding-cases.test.js and against the control-plane tests' FAKE site by control-plane/api/test/site-binding-cases.test.ts, which loads this same file by relative path (the control-plane workflow checks out the whole repository). Edit a rule on one side and the other side's run of this table fails.

_vocabulary.participant: member = a plain member of the trip site; organizer = a configured organizer; unknown = not a participant
_vocabulary.existing: none | actor | other_user | invite | actor_on_other_participant | actor_invite: what the site already holds for the participant being asked about (the actor is the control-plane user making the call; actor_invite = the actor already bound by THIS invite, the one a provision call names)
_vocabulary.holder: who can open the participant afterwards: actor | previous (whoever held it before) | nobody
_vocabulary.order: cases run in this order against one site; the invite case permanently consumes the second plain member, so it is last

adopt.name: a free plain member is bound to the actor
the same actor adopting again is not an error
a leftover binding of another account is replaced
an actor already bound to another participant is refused
a name that is not a participant is never bound
an invite-bound binding is never displaced

release.name: the actor releases its own binding
releasing what nobody holds is not an error
an invite-bound binding is never released through this path

_provision: The personal invite for an existing traveller (docs/specs/sprint-9/x-member-sign-in.md, AC-10): POST /api/internal/control-plane/participants binds an invite-redeeming account to an existing participant, with the invite's id on the binding. It differs from adopt in two ways: the binding is invite-bound (never displaced, never released through release), and a LEFTOVER claim binding on the name is replaced (the control plane has already checked, under its own lock, that no claim is live). Each provision case runs against a freshly started site, because an invite binding is permanent.

provision.name: a free plain member is bound to the invited account
the same invite again is not an error
a leftover claim binding of another account is replaced
another invite's binding is never displaced
an account already bound to another participant is refused
a name that is not a participant is never bound
